title: I made 20 playable game demos in ONE day using the LittleJS GPT!
author: Slackluster
selftext:
Try it yourself here and share your experience and results...

[https://chatgpt.com/g/g-67c7c080b5bc81919736bc8815836be6-make-games-with-littlejs](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-67c7c080b5bc81919736bc8815836be6-make-games-with-littlejs)

comments.author: __Maximum__
comments.body: How about 1 that is worth to play 10 minutes?

replies.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
replies.body: I believe this post was an open invitation for you to build one.

replies.author: EverythingBOffensive
replies.body: pretty much, ye can have any kind of game made if you have a lot of patience and willing to do some manual work for stuff the ai can't do.

replies.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
replies.body:
I agree.

People tend to forget that just a couple of years ago, AI was able to create exactly 0 of these "too simple" games. Give it couple of years and we will see much more advanced creations done all by AI alone.

replies.author: EverythingBOffensive
replies.body: its quite mind blowing how it can do this stuff now compared to a year ago. i tried to make games with it before and it was bad, but it was flawless at helping me make some insane never before made oblivion mods. Now I have it making 3d games. Its still a lot of work the more advanced it gets but its definitely getting there. I'd imagine the highest premium gpt can do tons more stuff with less errors.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: You've never played tetris for more then 10 minutes? All these demos were made with only a few prompts and you can continue to iterate on them to add more mechanics and tweak the gameplay. These can be used as a prototype to replace with better art, sound, and music. You can take the resulting code and continue working on it.

replies.author: ilikecdda-tilesets
replies.body: Why the hate? Hes just "adversiting" littlejs

replies.author: __Maximum__
replies.body: Because I don't think another platform in addition to 20 that does exactly the same thing is needed.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: Would you mind sharing some of those 20? I'd be happy to add them to my research.

replies.author: __Maximum__
replies.body: Any agentic framework, including open source ones, like cline or roo code with local models, or aistudio, or the corresponding offical platforms for minimax 2.1, glm 4.7... then manus, to name a few.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: Cool. Do any of those have a link where someone who does not know how to program can just type in a prompt and have it make a game for them?

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: Cool, what is the link? Do they use plain vanilla JS or a game engine? Why not use LittleJS  game engine?

replies.author: __Maximum__
replies.body: Some just JS, others anything you want.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
Cool, still no link, but it would be better if they used a game engine. Both because it is easer to develop into a larger game and also easier for the AI to implement via engine framework rather then programming every low level bit of code.

So it sounds like those other platforms would benefit from improvements made to LittleJS and other open source JavaScript game engines. I'm glad we could agree on something.

comments.author: MacIntoic
comments.body: What's the point? These games already exist. If you want to advertise it, prove that you're capable of creating original ones with it.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
I'm not really advertising it, just offering it as a free tool. I'd actually prefer that other people use it to bring their own ideas to life. I am already a capable programmer and game developer so I don't typically vibe code to this extreme. But I'm also interested in improving the tech which I can only do with feedback from others.

Also, it may sound crazy to you but game devs often start with prototypes that are inspired by other games that already exist. In fact it is the rare exception for a game to be created out of nowhere where there was no game before it that it clearly copied the basic formula of.

replies.author: oVerde
replies.body: Exactly, you can only make what is already well know and built, this is how LLMs work 🤷‍♂️

comments.author: EverythingBOffensive
comments.body: damn they came out pretty nice. did you know u can also make 3d games with panda3d and python?

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: You can also use Three.js in JavaScript to make pretty cool 3D stuff but I am mostly focused on improving how LittleJS engine interfaces with LLMs.

comments.author: RubikTetris
comments.body: I wonder if the ai was able to make them only because they are so common and popular.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
Yeah, that is a big factor I am sure. The more times a game has been implemented the more code the AI will have seen of it. But really the goal is not to remake Tetris. This is meant to be a start not an end.

The main use case would to have the AI make a small prototype based on something it knows, then use that as a starting point to develop it into an original game.

For example, many devs want to make a platforming game. So you might start by asking it to make mario bros. Then after the core is working add custom mechanics to it. Bring it out of ChatGPT and continue iterating with copilot or cursor. Add art and music. Etc.
